residuals-s1.title: Car age and price: the line and its residuals
residuals-s1.text: The dealer's 16 used cars of one model (age in years, price in thousands of dollars) with the regression line $\widehat{\text{price}} = 29.56 - 1.905(\text{age})$. The bottom panel is the residual plot. (Invented data.)

residuals-s2.title: Iced drinks and temperature: the residual plot
residuals-s2.text: A cafe records the daily high temperature (°F) and the number of iced drinks sold on 12 days. Its regression line is $\hat{y} = -114.8 + 3.41x$. The residual plot is below. (Invented data.)

plot.label: Residual plot of the iced drink line: 12 residuals between about minus 7.5 and 5.4 scattered above and below the zero line with no pattern, across temperatures from 62 to 91 degrees

items.q: The 5-year-old car is listed at 17.6 thousand dollars. What is its residual, in thousands of dollars? Give two decimal places.

mistakes.why: That is predicted minus actual. A residual is actual minus predicted, $y - \hat{y}$.
That is the predicted price, $\hat{y}$. The residual is the actual price minus it.

items.q: Interpret the residual of about $-2.44$ for the 5-year-old car.

why.correct: Residual $= y - \hat{y}$; negative means the line overpredicts.
options: Right: a negative residual means the actual value is below the predicted value.
Negative means below the line: actual minus predicted is less than 0.
A residual is a gap between actual and predicted, not a yearly change.
Every point has a residual; a moderate one is normal scatter.
It sold for about 2,438 dollars below the line's prediction
Its price is about 2,438 dollars more than the line predicts
The car lost about 2,438 dollars of value each year
The line is wrong for this car and should be refit without it

items.q: What does the residual plot show about using a line for these data?

why.correct: A good line leaves residuals scattered randomly around 0, with no pattern.
options: Residuals of any line have both signs. What matters is whether they form a pattern.
Size alone does not settle it; the curved pattern shows a line is the wrong shape.
Negative residuals are expected. The problem is the curved pattern.
Right: a pattern in the residuals means the relationship is curved, so a line misses it in a systematic way.
A line is appropriate, because the residuals are both positive and negative
A line is appropriate, because the residuals are small
A line is not appropriate, because some residuals are negative
A line is not appropriate: the residuals form a U-shaped curve

items.q: For which cars does the line underpredict the price?

why.correct: Underpredict: positive residual, actual above predicted.
options: The oldest cars also have positive residuals.
A fitted line still misses individual points both ways.
Right: their residuals are positive, so the actual prices are above the line.
Those residuals are negative: the line overpredicts them.
The newest cars, but not the oldest
No cars, since the line is fit to the data
The newest and the oldest cars
The cars aged 4 to 7 years

items.q: A buyer uses the line to predict the price of a 10-year-old car. Based on the residual plot, what is likely?

why.correct: A pattern in the residuals tells you where predictions are biased.
options: Ages up to 11 are in the data, so 10 is not extrapolation.
Prices fall, but more slowly than the line says for old cars, so it underpredicts.
Right: the curve lifts the oldest prices above the line, so the line tends to underpredict there.
Inside the data, but where the residuals show a systematic positive gap.
The prediction is impossible, since 10 years is extrapolation
The prediction is probably too high, since prices fall with age
Probably too low: old cars have positive residuals
The prediction is about right, since 10 years is inside the data

items.q: What does the residual plot suggest?

why.correct: No pattern in the residual plot: a linear model is appropriate.
options: Random ups and downs are expected; a systematic curve would be the problem.
Residuals are rarely 0. A random scatter around 0 is what a good fit looks like.
Negative residuals appear with any line. There is no curved pattern here.
Right: no curve and no change in spread, so the line captures the pattern.
A line is not reasonable, because the residuals go up and down
A line is not reasonable, because the residuals are not 0
A curve would fit better, because some residuals are negative
A line is reasonable: residuals scatter randomly around 0

items.q: On the 80°F day, the cafe sold 160 iced drinks. What is the residual for that day?

options: That is predicted minus actual. Residual is actual minus predicted.
That is the temperature, not a residual.
That is the predicted number of drinks, not the residual.
About -2.3 drinks
About 2.3 drinks
About 80 drinks
About 157.7 drinks

items.q: The day with the most negative residual, about $-7.5$, was 77°F. What does that residual mean?

why.correct: Interpret a residual in context: actual compared with predicted.
options: The line predicts drinks, not temperature.
A residual is one day's gap, not a rate.
Right: negative residual, actual below predicted.
A negative residual means fewer than predicted.
The temperature was about 7.5 degrees lower than predicted that day
Sales dropped by 7.5 drinks per degree that day
About 7.5 fewer iced drinks were sold than the line predicts
The cafe sold about 7.5 more iced drinks than predicted

items.q: A line predicts a student's exam score from homework average: $\hat{y} = 12.5 + 0.8x$. A student with a homework average of 40 scored 47. Write the expression for the residual, then evaluate it.

mistakes.why: That is predicted minus actual. A residual is actual minus predicted.
Keep the prediction in parentheses: subtract the whole $\hat{y} = 12.5 + 0.8(40)$.

items.q: A point has a residual of 0. Where is it?

options: Being at $\bar{y}$ does not make the residual 0 unless the line passes through it there.
A residual of 0 can happen at any $x$.
Far from the line means a large residual.
Right: its actual value equals its predicted value.
At the mean of $y$
At $x = 0$
Far from the line
Exactly on the regression line

items.q: A residual plot shows residuals spread out more and more as $x$ increases, like a fan. What does this mean?

why.correct: Fan shape: spread of the residuals changes with $x$.
options: A curve shows up as a bend in the residuals. A fan shows growing spread.
A fan shape says nothing about $r$ being 0.
Right: the line's typical error changes with $x$, so predictions for large $x$ are less reliable.
The residuals are largest there, so the fit is worst there.
The relationship is curved
The correlation is exactly 0
Predictions are less precise for large $x$, since the scatter grows
The line fits perfectly for large $x$

items.q: A line overpredicts a value. What is the sign of its residual?

options: Positive means the actual value is above the prediction, an underprediction.
Zero means the prediction is exact.
The sign depends only on whether the point is above or below the line.
Right: overpredicting means $\hat{y} > y$, so $y - \hat{y} < 0$.
Positive
Zero
It depends on the slope
Negative

items.q: A line predicts weight (kg) from height (cm). In what units are its residuals?

why.correct: Residuals are in the units of the response.
options: That is the unit of the slope.
Residuals have the units of $y$.
Residuals are vertical gaps, in the units of the response.
Right: a residual is a difference of two $y$ values, so it has the units of $y$.
Kilograms per centimeter
No units
Centimeters
Kilograms

items.q: Which residual plot pattern means a straight line fits the data well?

why.correct: A good residual plot is a patternless horizontal band.
options: A trend in the residuals means the line has missed a pattern.
Right: no curve, no fan, nothing systematic.
A U shape means the data curve.
A fan means the spread changes with $x$.
Points rising steadily from left to right
Random scatter around 0 with even spread
Points forming a clear U shape
Points fanning out from left to right

items.q: For a set of data, $r = 0.95$, but the residual plot shows a clear curved pattern. What should you conclude?

why.correct: Judge the form from the residual plot, not from $r$.
options: A strong correlation does not guarantee the right form. The residual plot is the check.
Right: a high $r$ can come from curved data; the residual plot shows the line misses the curve.
Both are right: $r$ measures linear strength, and a strong curve can still give a high $r$.
The relationship is strong; it is just curved.
The line is a good model, because $r$ is close to 1
A curved model would describe the data better, even though $r$ is high
The residual plot is probably wrong, since $r$ is high
The data have no relationship
